newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tropical storm Guillermo stirs off Mexico's coast.
newsitem.headline: Tropical storm Guillermo stirs off Mexico's coast.

text.p: Tropical storm Guillermo, almost stationary off Mexico's Pacific coast, is bringing widespread rain to southern Mexico, the National Meterological Service said Thursday.
Guillermo's eye was seen centered 255 miles (410 km) south of Puerto Angel in Oaxaca state at 1300 local (1800 GMT), according to the weather service estimates.
"It is expected that Tropical storm Guillmero will pick up steam gradually," the service reported in an update.
Guillermo is currently registering winds of 41 mph (65 km/h) and gusts of 53 mph (85 km/h) and was expected to gain force to sustained winds of 47 mph (75 km/h) and gusts of 56 mph (90 km/h).
Shipping warnings were out in the Golfo de Tehuantepec because of the rains, winds and sea swells, the service added.

Oaxaca is one of Mexico's top coffee producing states and neighbors Chiapas, which is traditionally Mexico's biggest producer state. Both states also have other agricultural output such as sugar and grains.
